title: When the Ghost Breaks
premise: Silas Dunmore, a crash investigator whose family died in row twelve of Flight 447, has spent years living off-grid under the protection of a shadowy network that trained her to read wreckage like scripture. When the safe house she's hidden in for a decade is listed online — interior photos included, down to her mother's teacup on the sill — Silas realizes the network that made her is now selling her. Following the listing's digital trail to a border town where the checkpoint shifts change at dawn, she discovers the network's founder intends to auction her skills, and her inherited file of unsolved attributed crashes, to the highest bidder. To survive, Silas must burn the network from inside its own archive, choosing at last between the belonging it promised and the self she buried. The story ends with the archive in flames, the founder dead by his own contingency plan, and Silas walking through the checkpoint under her own name for the first time.
about_author: Beatrix Brightwater is the pen name of a former aviation insurance analyst who spent eleven years reading accident reports before turning to fiction. She writes from a farmhouse that appears on no maps, and insists every thriller she writes begins with a real document she can no longer discuss.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Silas investigates a commuter crash in fog, cataloging debris with clinical precision while flashbacks reveal her family died in row twelve of an unattributed crash years ago. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into method; she trusts wreckage more than people.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: A colleague sends Silas a real estate link as a joke. The safe house — her safe house — is listed with interior photos: her books, her mother's teacup, the scratch marks she made counting days. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: cold vertigo; invisibility was an illusion someone maintained and has now withdrawn.

chapters.title: Handler Ghosts
chapters.summary: Silas calls her handler, Marek, who goes silent mid-call. She flees the house hours before a 'buyer's viewing' arrives — two men photographing rooms that were never for sale. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into certainty that the network is liquidating assets, including her.

chapters.title: The Training File
chapters.summary: In a bus station locker, Silas retrieves her own training file, cached years ago: psychological profiles, induced traumas, the engineered grief that made her a perfect investigator. POV: Silas with brief archive-document interludes. Emotional beat: violated intimacy; her identity was a curriculum.

chapters.title: Marek's Confession
chapters.summary: Marek surfaces in person, half-drunk, admitting the network's founder, Aldous Vane, is dying and selling everything — safe houses, operatives' files, and Silas herself as a lot. He gives her a keycard before vanishing. POV: alternating Silas/Marek. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with reluctant loyalty.

chapters.title: The Auction Catalog
chapters.summary: The keycard opens a darknet catalog: Lot 31, 'The Dunmore Asset,' complete with her psych profile and a reserve price. Bidding opens in nine days, timed to the border checkpoint shift change. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: being priced is worse than being hunted.

chapters.title: Border Town
chapters.summary: Silas travels to Kesselstadt, the drab border town where the network archives its paper originals. She poses as an insurance adjuster and maps the checkpoint's shift rotations. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: hunter's patience rekindled; the investigator turns her methods on her makers.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Silas recruits Ines, a disillusioned network archivist who digitized the files and knows the vault layout. Ines agrees only after seeing her own name in the auction catalog. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: two women recognizing they were inventory, not employees.

chapters.title: What Vane Built
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Silas's recruitment after the crash, Vane's paternal charisma, the first time she was told her grief was 'an asset.' POV: Silas (past). Emotional beat: seduction of belonging — the network felt like family because it replaced one.

chapters.title: Counter-Bidder
chapters.summary: A rival buyer, arms-adjacent financier Corvin Hale, approaches Silas openly, offering to buy her freedom if she'll work for him. She realizes he's bidding partly to spite Vane. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: temptation — escape offered as another form of ownership.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Recon
chapters.summary: Silas and Ines time the checkpoint shifts: a ninety-minute window when the night rotation overlaps and the manifest checks lapse. They test it with a decoy courier carrying worthless paper. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: fragile competence; the plan holds, barely.

chapters.title: The Vault Door
chapters.summary: Ines gets them into the archive sublevel, but the physical vault requires biometric input — Vane himself, or his designated heir. Silas learns there is an heir: a woman raised as Vane's daughter. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the architecture of power always needs a bloodline.

chapters.title: The Heir
chapters.summary: Silas tracks the heir, Livia Vane, expecting a monster and finding a prisoner — a woman groomed to inherit a machine she despises. Livia reveals the auction is also Vane's succession test. POV: Livia. Emotional beat: mirror recognition; both women were raised as instruments.

chapters.title: Lot 31 Opens
chapters.summary: Bidding goes live early. Hale drives the price up; a state actor enters quietly. Vane summons Silas personally — not to capture her, but to offer her partnership: inherit the network, keep the belonging. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the devil offering exactly what she always wanted.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Founder
chapters.summary: Silas dines with Vane in the archive's upper residence. He shows her the original file on Flight 447 — the crash that killed her family was network-attributed, covered for a client. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing; the grief that built her was manufactured twice over.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Vane offers her the network and the truth about row twelve in exchange for killing the auction and executing his enemies. Silas pretends to negotiate while Livia copies the vault credentials. POV: alternating Silas/Livia. Emotional beat: performance of surrender masking design.

chapters.title: Hale's Move
chapters.summary: Corvin Hale, losing the bid, tries to seize the archive by force with hired contractors, forcing everyone's timeline up. Marek returns to warn Silas and is shot covering her retreat. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: cost made flesh; loyalty repaid in blood.

chapters.title: The Burn Protocol
chapters.summary: Inside the vault, Silas and Livia trigger the network's own burn protocol — designed to destroy evidence of clients' crimes — while Ines exfiltrates the true Flight 447 file physically. Contractors breach the sublevel. POV: alternating trio. Emotional beat: using the machine's power against itself.

chapters.title: Vane's Contingency
chapters.summary: Cornered above the burning archive, Vane triggers his final contingency — a dead-man switch meant to kill whoever betrayed him. It misfires on his own biometrics as the fire reaches the residence. He dies amid the records he ruled by. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: not triumph but hollow clarity; power devours its owner.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes
chapters.summary: With the facility in chaos and Hale's contractors sweeping the perimeter, Silas, Livia, and Ines make for the checkpoint inside the shift-change window, carrying the Flight 447 file and nothing else. A contractor recognizes Silas at the last gate. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: terror and resolve fused; the past literally in her hands.

chapters.title: Crossing
chapters.summary: Silas talks her way through the checkpoint using her real name and genuine documents — the one thing no forged network identity could do. On the far side, she releases the Flight 447 file to journalists and aviation authorities. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: the quiet enormity of being legible, accountable, free.

chapters.title: After the Fire
chapters.summary: Months later: hearings begin, Hale is indicted, Livia dismantles what remains of the network legally. Silas visits a memorial wall and adds her family's names beside the truth of how they died. She takes a new case — ordinary, unattributed by no one. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed as memory, not mission; belonging chosen, not assigned.
